title: Incremental envelope resume and parser-hint guided recovery acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
background: Customers are using streamed structured responses with downstream tool invocation. When partial emissions are interrupted (network, model crash, or early stop), customers need a reliable way to resume, repair, or safely fallback without duplicating side-effects on tool endpoints. Previous PM work defined envelopes and checkpoints, but field feedback shows inconsistent resume behavior across parsers and client SDKs. This ticket defines acceptance criteria for: (1) an envelope resume protocol anchored by stable IDs and soft checkpoints, (2) parser hints to enable tolerant recovery and partial repair heuristics, and (3) explicit error modes and operator-visible telemetry.
goals: 1) Define deterministic acceptance criteria for resumed streaming that minimizes duplicate tool calls and maximizes recoverability. 2) Specify parser-hint fields in the envelope that clients and SDKs can consume for safe partial-JSON repair. 3) Define testable error modes and SLOs for resume latency and correctness.
scope_included:
- Envelope-level resume semantics (resume_token, envelope_id, sequence_hint)
- Parser hint fields (frame_type, tolerant_mode, expected_schema_version)
- Tool call idempotency guidance and required observable markers
- Acceptance tests and automated E2E scenarios for common failure classes
- Telemetry definitions: resumed_count, resumed_success_rate, duplicate_tool_call_rate
scope_excluded:
- New transport-layer protocol (we use existing streaming API)
- Changes to existing model output formats that break current consumers
- Implementing SDKs across all languages (initial focus: JS + Python)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Resume determinism: Given an interrupted stream with an envelope containing envelope_id and resume_token, the platform can replay tokens from the last acknowledged checkpoint and produce the same sequence of meaningful JSON frames or a validated repaired sequence.
2) Idempotent tool calls: Tool calls emitted by the model must include call_id and idempotency_key. On resume, the platform must not re-emit a tool call unless the previous call status is unknown and at-least-once semantics are explicitly requested.
3) Parser hints respected: Envelopes may include parser_hint.tolerant_mode and parser_hint.fragment_anchor which SDKs can use to attempt local repair. Acceptance requires SDKs to demonstrate repair for truncated JSON fragments up to 256 bytes using the hint fields in 90% of synthetic failure runs.
4) Clear error modes: Resume outcome must be categorized into one of: resumed_clean, resumed_repaired, cannot_recover. Each stream must emit a final envelope.status value.
5) Telemetry: resumed_success_rate >= 95% on synthetic network-interruption tests; duplicate_tool_call_rate <= 0.1% for resumed_clean streams.
6) Backpressure and checkpoint guarantees: Checkpoints (soft) must be emitted at least every 250ms or every 512 tokens, whichever comes first, and are used as resume anchors.
7) Operator playbook: When cannot_recover is reached, the system surfaces an operator action in Console with envelope_id, last_checkpoint, and a suggested remediation step.
8) Security: resume_token must be opaque and short-lived; logs must not contain raw resume_token values.
test_plan:
Automated suites and manual e2e: 
- Unit: validate envelope schema and parser_hint fields.
- Integration: run 1,000 synthetic interruption tests combining model stops, network drops, and runtime restarts across CPU/GPU hosts. Expect >= 95% resumed_success_rate.
- Tool-idempotency tests: simulate tool-side acknowledgements and verify dedup semantics against stored call_id/idempotency_key.
- SDK repair harness: JS + Python test harness attempts repair for truncated JSON fragments using parser_hint; report success rate and diagnostic examples.
- Chaos test: random chunk truncation during streaming in staging with observability enabled; validate telemetry and operator alerts.
- Regression: ensure existing streaming consumers without parser_hint continue to function (no breaking changes).
test_cases:
TC-01 truncated-json-repair: model emits JSON frame, stream truncated mid-object -> SDK uses fragment_anchor + tolerant_mode to reconstruct valid JSON and resume tool call mapping. Expected: resumed_repaired, tool call dedup verified.
TC-02 missing-checkpoint: stream interrupted before first checkpoint -> platform must resume from first available checkpoint; if none, mark cannot_recover and surface operator action.
TC-03 duplicate-suppression: resume after ack ambiguity -> if tool call status unknown and idempotency_key absent, platform must surface warning and default to fail-safe non-reemit behavior.
TC-04 large-replay: resume after 10s outage -> platform replays up to N tokens respecting latency SLO; acceptance requires replay latency < 2s for initial 50 tokens.
TC-05 parser-hint-version-mismatch: client receives expected_schema_version != client_supported -> client should request a soft-fallback or reject with clear error code.
success_metrics:
- resumed_success_rate >= 95% in synthetic tests
- duplicate_tool_call_rate <= 0.1% for resumed_clean streams
- mean resume latency (first token) <= 200ms after reconnection in 95th percentile
- operator interventions per 10k resumed streams < 1
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): enable envelope resume in staging with 5% of internal traffic and SDK repair enabled. Monitor telemetry for 72 hours.
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in customer SDKs and early access tenants, increase to 25% traffic, add additional checks for idempotency across Dedicated capacity.
Phase 3 (GA): default behavior for all hosted streams, SDKs released as stable. Provide migration guide and opt-out flag for customers who prefer fail-fast semantics.

open_questions:
- Should resume_token be revocable per-session or per-request? (tradeoff: revocable increases security but complicates long-running clients)
- What is the maximum fragment size we guarantee repair for? Proposal: 256 bytes.
- Do we require idempotency_key for all tool calls or allow best-effort for legacy models? Proposal: require for all new model adapters, recommend for legacy with warnings.
notes_and_decisions:
2026-03-14: Decided to implement soft checkpoints (emit frequency) rather than heavy-weight persistent offsets to balance cost and recoverability.
2026-03-15: Agreed parser_hint will be advisory; SDKs may decline to repair if local policy forbids.
Tradeoffs captured: stronger guarantees (strict durability) would require storing per-connection offsets and increase storage/IO costs; chosen soft-checkpoint approach is optimistic and relies on model emission frequency.
Review feedback: SRE requested metrics for replay latency and worst-case token backlog; added mean resume latency goal.
